title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used for compressing a teacher model to reduce its inference cost and memory footprint, by training a smaller student model. On-policy distillation trains the student on its own self-generated outputs (rather than teacher-generated data), directly addressing distribution shift between student trajectories and offline teacher data.

title: DistillSpec: Improving Speculative Decoding via Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by employing a faster draft model for generating multiple tokens, which are then verified by the larger target model. DistillSpec proposes training the draft model via knowledge distillation using on-policy data sampled from the target model's distribution, directly aligning student trajectories with the teacher to reduce distribution mismatch.

title: A Good Learner can Teach Better: Teacher-Student Collaborative Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a technique used to transfer knowledge from a larger teacher model into a smaller student model. This work proposes a collaborative framework where the student's learning progress iteratively informs and improves the teacher's teaching strategy, enabling bidirectional feedback between teacher and student during distillation.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Despite their remarkable capabilities, large language models (LLMs) often produce responses containing factual inaccuracies due to their sole reliance on parametric knowledge. Self-RAG trains a single LM that adaptively retrieves, generates, and critiques text passages using self-generated special reflection tokens, trained on self-generated data from a critic model — a form of iterative self-distillation from model-generated trajectories.

title: Boosting of Thoughts: Trial-and-Error Problem Solving with Large Language Models
abstract: The reasoning performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on a wide range of problems critically relies on chain-of-thought prompting. This work proposes iterative trial-and-error reasoning where the LLM learns from its own self-generated mistakes across attempts, analogous to on-policy improvement from student-generated trajectories.

title: DataEnvGym: Data Generation Agents in Teacher Environments with Student Feedback
abstract: The process of creating training data to teach models is currently driven by humans, who manually analyze model weaknesses and plan how to create data to address them. DataEnvGym proposes data generation agents that operate in teacher environments, using iterative student feedback to guide on-policy data generation — directly addressing distribution shift between student trajectories and static datasets.

title: Regressing the Relative Future: Efficient Policy Optimization for Multi-turn RLHF
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success at tasks like summarization that involve a single turn of interaction. However, they can still struggle at multi-turn tasks. This work proposes on-policy credit assignment via regressing relative future returns from student-generated multi-turn trajectories, enabling efficient policy optimization beyond single-turn RLHF.

title: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), optimized through human feedback, have rapidly emerged as a leading paradigm for developing intelligent conversational agents. This work proposes action-based contrastive self-training, where the LLM iteratively improves clarification behavior using contrastive pairs drawn from self-generated multi-turn conversation trajectories — an on-policy self-distillation approach.

title: When Context Returns: Toward Robust Internalization in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Recent work has shown that on-policy distillation can internalize privileged context into a student model so that the context is no longer needed at inference time. We identify context-induced degradation: reintroducing the original privileged context to the distilled student actually degrades its performance. We propose a lightweight consistency regularizer that anchors the student's no-context output via stop-gradient, then penalizes the context-conditioned output via forward KL divergence, achieving context removability.

title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) concentrates on style tokens rather than task-bearing ones due to privilege-induced style drift. RLCSD mitigates this by contrasting the teacher-student gap under a correct hint against that under a wrong hint, suppressing style shift and yielding a signal concentrated on task-bearing tokens. Consistently outperforms GRPO and prior OPSD methods on Qwen3 and Olmo-3.

title: The Role of Feedback Alignment in Self-Distillation
abstract: Studies context design for self-distillation: compares binary reward (GRPO), reference solution, and step-aligned critique. Step-aligned critique outperforms GRPO by 16.11 points and reference-solution-conditioned SD by 5.27 points (Avg@12). Per-token advantage analysis shows step-aligned feedback targets only tokens where reasoning fails.

title: Beyond Absolute Imitation: Anchored Residual Guidance for Privileged On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Introduces AR-OPD, a dual-view framework disentangling privileged supervision. Rather than enforcing strict full-view imitation, AR-OPD establishes a locally compatible anchor using a partially privileged teacher, isolating and injecting oracle foresight as a controlled residual. Outperforms full privileged OPD by 2.3 points and SFT by 7.9 points; reduces hindsight leakage by 21.7%.

title: Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Visual Feedback: Bridging Code and Visual Artifacts
abstract: Visual-SDPO is a self-distillation policy-optimization framework treating rendered visual feedback as privileged context for a weight-sharing teacher. Introduces Visual-Grounded Code Credit Weighting tracing detected defects back to responsible code statements. Combined with GRPO term; improves over zero-shot base by 10+ points and over GRPO by 2.4+ points on chart/UI/slide generation.

title: Escaping the KL Agreement Trap in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Identifies a persistent low-KL agreement trap in OPD: when the student drifts into an unrecoverable prefix, the teacher locally agrees with the degraded state, producing little corrective signal. Proposes KAT (KL Agreement Trap Termination), an online termination rule with dynamic training-adaptive threshold. Improves avg@k by 2.66% and pass@k by 3.43% while reducing rollout length by 59.73%.

title: Breaking the Tokenizer Barrier: On-Policy Distillation across Model Families
abstract: Existing OPD requires teacher and student to share the same tokenizer. This work enables OPD across model families via a precise token-mapping algorithm, ensuring high-fidelity token-level signals propagate across different tokenizers. Cross-tokenizer OPD is significantly more compute-efficient than SFT baselines and unlocks broader teacher-student pairs.

title: PBSD: Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Credit Assignment
abstract: Proposes PBSD for fine-grained credit assignment under sparse final rewards in agentic tasks. Measures trajectory quality via posterior-to-prior probability ratio of the verified answer; applies Bayes' rule to convert answer-side ratio into a tractable likelihood ratio between student and privileged answer-conditioned teacher. Autoregressive decomposition yields turn-level credit signals identifying whether each intermediate turn supports or undermines the outcome.

title: SG-OPD: Sign-Gated On-Policy Distillation via Sign-Consistency Gating and Phased Teacher Sampling
abstract: OPD implicitly relies on trajectory-level alignment and uniform token-level teacher reliability. SG-OPD uses a binary verifier as trust signal at two granularities: phased teacher sampling mixes verifier-endorsed teacher rollouts at cold-start; sign-consistency gate extrapolates distillation updates on tokens where teacher agrees with verifier-correct direction. Average gains of 1.98 and 7.50 on math reasoning.

title: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation for MLLM Reasoning with Global Normalization (GNDPO)
abstract: Naive token-level distillation suffers from gradient instability due to magnitude misalignment in outlier states. Proposes GNDPO (Globally Normalized Distillation Policy Optimization) that transforms raw KL scores into batch-level relative advantages. Mitigates gradient explosions while retaining token-level guidance. Substantially improves training robustness on multimodal reasoning tasks.

title: Stage-1 Controls the Entropy Regime, Not the Outcome
abstract: Empirical study of two-stage post-training: OPD warm-start vs SFT. Finds Stage-1 primarily controls entropy regime rather than final performance. OPD enters RL with substantially higher policy entropy than SFT, but the downstream payoff is small and localized. OPD-warmed model has higher answer diversity and pass@16 at initialization, but advantage disappears after RL.

title: Thinking Without Images: Internalizing Visual Manipulation with On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: Proposes Imagine-OPD, an on-policy self-distillation framework to internalize 'Thinking with Images' into 'Thinking with Imagination'. A privileged teacher receives zoomed evidence views from annotated regions and supervises the model's imagination reasoning trajectories. No external teacher or high-quality demonstrations required. Achieves best average performance while significantly reducing inference overhead.

title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation
abstract: Identifies prefix failure as a structural cause underlying OPD: dense per-token supervision induces a bimodal teacher mixture and fragmented gradients. TRD moves beyond token-level interventions to trajectory-level corrections, revising the student's rollout under teacher guidance within on-policy support. Also applies to OPSD (parameter-sharing variant). Consistently outperforms prior baselines across benchmarks and model scales.

title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Characterizes OPD update trajectories in parameter space vs SFT and RLVR. OPD occupies a relaxed off-principal regime and exhibits subspace locking—cumulative updates rapidly enter a narrow low-dimensional channel. Constraining training to early-formed update subspace preserves OPD but degrades SFT. OPD induces its own update geometry distinct from both SFT and RLVR.

title: Teaching the Way, Not the Answer: Privileged Tutoring Distillation for Multimodal Policy Optimization
abstract: PTD-PO provides dense guidance without exposing the answer to the student policy. Constructs structured privileged hints from spatial attention guidance and intermediate reasoning steps via in-context learning for step-wise token-distribution supervision. Introduces Top-K Jensen-Shannon divergence objective for stability under distribution shift. Outperforms RLVR and distillation baselines on 2B–8B LVLMs.

title: Learning Visual Spatial Planning from Symbolic State via Modality-Gap-Aware Self-Distillation
abstract: MGSD addresses the perception-reasoning modality gap in visual planning. Cold-start grounding stage plus privileged teacher transferring planning via on-policy distillation with symbolic states supervising visual rollout prefixes. Symbolic data used strictly during training; inference is purely visual. Raises macro average by 19.3% and 18.4% on 4B and 8B backbones.

title: ViCuR: Visual Cues as Recoverable Privilege for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Replaces answer-side privilege in multimodal OPD with visual cues derived from the same visual input available at inference (recoverable evidence). Introduces lightweight sink-token cross-attention cue recovery module. Consistently improves over answer-based on-policy self-distillation by +1.19/+1.24 and OPD baselines by +0.64/+1.08 on seven benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-2B and 8B.

title: Reinforcement Learning from Rich Feedback with Distributional DAgger
abstract: DistIL (Distributional DAgger) studies rich feedback through distributional variant of classic imitation learning. Shows prior RL with self-distillation objectives (reverse KL, Jensen-Shannon) fail to guarantee monotonic policy improvement. Forward cross-entropy admits monotonic policy improvement and optimizes a lower bound on teacher-weighted likelihood of success. Improves over RLVR and RL+self-distillation baselines across science, coding, math.

title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient
abstract: SDPG combines group-relative verifier advantages with normalized standard deviation, exact full-vocabulary on-policy self-distillation (reverse KL auxiliary loss), and reference-policy KL regularization. Improves stability and performance over RLVR and self-distillation baselines.

title: World Models Meet Language Models: On the Complementarity of Concrete and Abstract Reasoning
abstract: Proposes PF-OPSD (Privileged-Future On-Policy Self-Distillation) for controlled concrete reasoning. During training, ground-truth future videos and answers serve only as teacher-side privileged context to evaluate on-policy concrete-reasoning trajectories; deployable student never observes true futures at test time. Outperforms baseline by 10.6% and 10.9% on two benchmarks.

title: When Should the Teacher Move? Temporal Coupling and Stability in Self On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Systematically studies teacher update schedule in self-OPD. Establishes isolation periods (complete teacher freezing between updates) as the key structural property for stable learning, not teacher age. Identifies state-oblivious collapse: clock-driven refresh can catastrophically copy a transiently drifting student. Proposes CGTR (Consolidation-Gated Teacher Refresh) achieving zero collapse across all four tasks.

title: Constitutional On-Policy Safe Distillation
abstract: Safety OPSD suffers from collapse: constitutional conditioning contracts teacher distribution toward short, overly conservative responses; Reverse KL amplifies this into reduced expressiveness. Formalizes as geometric leakage under safety boundaries. COPSD uses Cross-SFT cold-start then constitution-conditioned on-policy distillation. Achieves stronger safety-helpfulness trade-off than baselines on 12 benchmarks.

title: Filter, Then Reweight: Rethinking Optimization Granularity in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: FiRe-OPD jointly adjusts supervision signals at both trajectory and token levels. First filters trajectories to remove low-quality rollouts, then applies soft reweighting to emphasize informative tokens. Soft-weighting mitigates information loss vs hard token selection. Validates in strong-to-weak, single-teacher, and multi-teacher settings; +6.25 on AIME 2024 and +18.81 on Miner over token-level OPD methods.

title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment
abstract: Argues safety features are sparse in output distribution, requiring localized rather than global modification. SafeSteer constructs safety teacher via activation steering, develops safety token selection algorithm, and restricts reverse KL penalty to safety tokens. Achieves strong safety on 7 benchmarks with minimal degradation on 5 general benchmarks using only 100 harmful samples.

title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification
abstract: OmniOPD enables OPD with proprietary black-box teachers by replacing logit matching with Monte Carlo rollout-based continuous semantic similarity over multi-token chunks. Peak-entropy scheduler concentrates supervision at high-uncertainty reasoning forks. Dirichlet-Multinomial prior and base-model KL anchor bound variance. +28.64% on math over standard OPD; when using Claude-4.5-Haiku/Gemini-2.5-Flash teachers, additional +9.54% over open-weight teacher.

title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
abstract: TrOPD addresses OPD instability under large teacher-student distribution divergence. Performs OPD only in trust regions where teacher provides reliable supervision; applies gradient clipping/masking/forward-KL for outlier regions; encourages exploration toward reliable regions via off-policy guidance from teacher prefixes. Consistently outperforms OPD, EOPD, REOPOLD on math, code, and general benchmarks.

title: OPD+: Rethinking the Advantage Design for On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Proves the standard stop-gradient design in OPD leads to biased estimates of the reward objective and corresponding gradient for general f-divergence functions. Proposes OPD+, a corrected version supporting various f-divergences. Provides a generic optimization framework based on f-divergence. Demonstrates improved performance over KL baseline on math reasoning and tool-use benchmarks.

title: Internalize the Temperature: On-Policy Self-Distillation as Policy Reheater for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: TS-OPSD internalizes the exploratory effect of temperature into model parameters after entropy collapse. Constructs self-teacher by applying high-temperature scaling to the model's own logits, then distills back into the student. No external teacher, privileged data, or additional inference cost. Policy reheating yields stronger RL initialization than standard continued RL or rollout-level temperature reheating on Qwen3-4B/8B-Base.

title: Robust Reasoning via Dynamic Token Selection for Distribution-Aligned Self-Distillation
abstract: DASD observes that rewriting data contains high-PPL tokens from two sources: beneficial logical corrections and harmful stylistic drift. Uses an answer-aware reference model to generate candidate tokens and dynamically filters by base model confidence, preserving logical knowledge while suppressing distribution-misaligned style noise. Consistently outperforms baselines on math, code, and commonsense reasoning.

title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Steering Gradients for Visual Grounding
abstract: Mathematically decomposes VLM distillation loss into language prior and visual grounding components, showing gradient vectors are nearly orthogonal. Standard optimization follows a suboptimal compromise. Introduces VGS (Visual Gradient Steering) that dynamically reorients update vector to prioritize visual subspace. Significantly outperforms standard monolithic OPD on multimodal reasoning benchmarks.

title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance
abstract: Shows ~30% of high-loss tokens in OPD are surface-form mismatches rather than reasoning forks. TOPD uses near-future trajectory information to identify truly divergent states and distributes guidance across multiple future tokens. Suppressing non-divergent high-loss tokens improves OPD from 47.8% to 48.2%; TOPD further improves to 52.2% (AIME24: 60.0→63.3%, AIME25: 46.7→53.3%).

title: CAST: Non-Privileged Clipped Asymmetric Self-Teaching with Advantage Flipping for GRPO
abstract: CAST is an answer-free self-distillation method for GRPO-style RLVR using stop-gradient self-teacher to shape token-level advantages by trajectory correctness. Applies bidirectional local advantage sign reversal: teacher-negative tokens in correct trajectories get negative advantages; teacher-positive tokens in incorrect trajectories get bounded positive local advantages. Handles zero-variance all-correct/all-wrong groups via sign-constrained base advantages.

title: Are Full Rollouts Necessary for On-Policy Distillation?
abstract: Identifies rollout horizon as a key bottleneck in OPD. Unlike RLVR, OPD does not require a final answer reward, so full rollouts may be unnecessary. POPD (Progressive OPD) gradually expands rollout horizon; Truncated OPD (TOPD) permanently distills on reliable truncated rollouts. POPD improves training efficiency by up to 3x; TOPD matches full OPD using only 10% of rollout horizon.

title: Trust-Region Behavior Blending for On-Policy Distillation
abstract: TRB is a warmup method replacing early rollout policy with the closest-to-teacher behavior policy inside a student-centered KL trust region, while keeping the per-prefix reverse-KL OPD loss unchanged. KL budget is annealed to zero so training returns to pure student rollouts after warmup. Attains strongest average among compared methods in two math-reasoning distillation settings.

title: Distilling LLM Feedback for Lean Theorem Proving
abstract: Feedback Distillation trains the model to match its own distribution conditioned on privileged feedback from a language model, providing token-level supervision with external knowledge injection. Maintains greater trajectory diversity than GRPO (higher policy entropy, better pass@k scaling) for Lean4 theorem proving. Initializing GRPO from Feedback Distillation checkpoint outperforms either method alone.

title: OISD: On-Policy Internal Self-Distillation of Language Models
abstract: OISD transfers on-policy predictive signals from the final layer to intermediate representations. Final layer acts as detached internal teacher for selected intermediate layers via logit alignment (reasoning behaviors) and attention alignment (attention patterns), both without external privileged information. Combined with GRPO using signed advantage-weighted Jensen-Shannon alignment. Substantial consistent improvements over strong RL baselines on four math tasks.

title: Skill-Conditioned Gated Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
abstract: SGSD formulates skill-based self-distillation as teacher hypothesis validation. Retrieves skill-mistake pairs, constructs multi-teacher pool, lets all skill-conditioned teachers score the same plain-prompt student rollout. Verifier validates each teacher's polarity; gated objective distills informative teacher-student disagreements while suppressing uncertain signals. Outperforms GRPO by 6.2% and OPSD by 1.7% on AIME24/25/HMMT25 (Qwen3-1.7B).

title: Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation under Large Policy Divergence
abstract: Identifies critical limitation of RKL-based OPD: under large teacher-student policy divergence, RL-driven exploration produces trajectories outside teacher distribution, resulting in uninformative negative feedback. TGPO uses teacher to directly guide token-level generation conditioning on student-generated contexts, combined with RLVR-style trajectory-level rewards. Consistently outperforms existing RKL-based OPD methods and remains robust across different teacher models.

title: Crosslingual On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning
abstract: COPSD transfers a model's own high-resource reasoning behavior to low-resource languages. Same model acts as student (sees low-resource problem) and teacher (receives privileged crosslingual context including English translation and reference solution). Full-distribution token-level divergence on student's own rollouts provides dense supervision. Consistently improves mathematical reasoning across 17 low-resource African languages, substantially outperforming GRPO.

title: SOD: Step-wise On-policy Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
abstract: Applies OPD to tool-integrated reasoning (TIR) agents. Identifies that erroneous tool calls cascade across reasoning steps, amplifying divergence and making teacher supervision unreliable. SOD adaptively reweights distillation strength at each step based on step-level divergence. Attenuates misleading signals in high-divergence regions while preserving guidance in well-aligned states. 0.6B student achieves 26.13% on AIME 2025.

title: SCOPE: Signal-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation Enhancement with Dual-Path Adaptive Weighting
abstract: SCOPE routes on-policy rollouts by correctness into two paths: for incorrect trajectories, teacher-perplexity-weighted KL distillation prioritizes instances where teacher demonstrates corrective capability; for correct trajectories, student-perplexity-weighted MLE concentrates reinforcement on low-confidence capability-boundary samples. Both paths use group-level normalization. Average relative improvement of 11.42% in Avg@32 and 7.30% in Pass@32 over competitive baselines.

title: HDPO: Hybrid Distillation Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation
abstract: HDPO augments standard RL with privileged self-distillation targeting cliff prompts (all rollouts fail). Identifies prompts where all rollouts fail, generates privileged rollouts by providing ground-truth information, filters for correct solutions, and distills teacher's token-level distribution into student. Teacher and student share same weights, bounding realizability gap. Proves R=1 filtered privileged generation recovers optimal KL-regularized RL policy in hard-threshold limit.

title: X-OPD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Distillation for Capability Alignment in Speech LLMs
abstract: X-OPD aligns Speech LLM capabilities to text-based counterparts. Speech LLM explores its own distribution via on-policy rollouts; text-based teacher evaluates trajectories and provides token-level feedback distilling capabilities into student's multi-modal representations. Significantly narrows the gap in complex tasks while preserving the model's inherent capabilities.

title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
abstract: On-Policy Context Distillation (OPCD) trains a student on its own generated trajectories while minimizing reverse KL against a context-conditioned teacher. Covers system-prompt internalization, experiential-knowledge distillation, and cross-size distillation. Consistently outperforms off-policy baselines on math, text-games, and domain tasks.

title: Speculative Knowledge Distillation: Bridging the Teacher-Student Gap Through Interleaved Sampling
abstract: SKD: student proposes tokens, teacher replaces low-ranked ones based on its distribution, generating on-the-fly high-quality training data aligned with student inference distribution. Addresses both off-policy distribution mismatch (SFT) and low-quality rollouts (on-policy KD). Evaluated on translation, summarization, math, instruction following.

title: Pangu Embedded: An Efficient Dual-system LLM Reasoner with Metacognition
abstract: Two-stage training: Stage 1 uses iterative distillation with inter-iteration model merging to aggregate complementary knowledge, followed by RL on Ascend clusters. Stage 2 introduces dual fast/slow thinking system with automatic complexity-aware mode selection. 7B model outperforms Qwen3-8B on AIME 2024, GPQA, LiveCodeBench.

title: Black-Box On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
abstract: Generative Adversarial Distillation (GAD): frames student as generator, trains discriminator to distinguish student vs. teacher responses—creates minimax game where discriminator acts as on-policy reward model co-evolving with student. Enables on-policy + black-box distillation without teacher logit access. Qwen2.5-14B trained with GAD reaches GPT-4-Chat parity on LMSYS-Chat eval.

title: TIP: Token Importance in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Two-axis token importance taxonomy: high-student-entropy tokens + low-entropy/high-teacher-student-divergence (overconfident-wrong) tokens. Entropy-based 50% token selection matches full training while reducing peak memory 47%. Training on <10% of tokens (overconfident subset) nearly matches full-token baseline. Validated on Qwen3, Llama, Qwen2.5 pairs.

title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
abstract: OEL: iterative online learning loop—extract experiential knowledge from deployment trajectories, consolidate into parameters via on-policy context distillation (no env access needed), repeat. Improves task accuracy and token efficiency across iterations on text-based games. Shows on-policy consistency between knowledge source and policy model is critical.

title: PACED: Distillation and On-Policy Self-Distillation at the Frontier of Student Competence
abstract: Weights each training problem by w(p)=p(1-p) where p is student's empirical pass rate—concentrates training on zone of proximal development. Theoretically proves Beta kernel is leading-order optimal from SNR boundary-collapse structure. SOTA on MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025 vs unweighted distillation (+8.2 pts) and AKL baseline (+3.6 pts). Two-stage forward-then-reverse KL schedule further boosts gains.

title: AlignDistil: Token-Level Language Model Alignment as Adaptive Policy Distillation
abstract: Proves RLHF objective is equivalent to token-level distillation where teacher distribution linearly combines DPO model and reference model logits. Uses contrastive DPO reward (normal + reverse DPO) to close accuracy gap vs. pure reward model. Token adaptive logit extrapolation avoids under/over-optimization per token.

title: VOLD: Reasoning Transfer from LLMs to Vision-Language Models via On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Combines GRPO with on-policy distillation for VLM reasoning transfer from text-only teacher. Shows cold-start SFT alignment is essential—without distributional alignment, OPD fails to provide meaningful guidance. Demonstrates VLMs need warm-start before on-policy distillation can be effective. Evaluated on MMMU-Pro, MathVision, MathVista, LogicVista.

title: SCOPE: Signal-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation Enhancement with Dual-Path Adaptive Weighting
abstract: Dual-path routing by rollout correctness: incorrect trajectories get teacher-perplexity-weighted KL distillation; correct trajectories get student-perplexity-weighted MLE on low-confidence samples. Group-level normalization calibrates weight distributions for difficulty variance. +11.42% Avg@32 and +7.30% Pass@32 over baselines on 6 reasoning benchmarks.

title: SIKeD: Self-guided Iterative Knowledge Distillation for mathematical reasoning
abstract: LLM teaches smaller model multiple reasoning strategies; smaller model uses self-generated on-policy outputs to choose best strategy per task. Iterative self-guided loop: each iteration decides how to combine LLM data with self-generated outputs. Unlike SFT distillation which forces a single strategy, SIKeD allows strategy selection. Significantly outperforms traditional distillation on various math reasoning datasets.

title: X-OPD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Distillation for Capability Alignment in Speech LLMs
abstract: Cross-modal OPD: Speech LLM explores own distribution via on-policy rollouts, text-based teacher evaluates trajectories and provides token-level feedback—distills text teacher capabilities into multi-modal student representations. Standard SFT and RL fail to close speech-to-text gap; X-OPD significantly narrows gap on complex tasks while preserving inherent capabilities.

title: Uni-OPD: Unifying On-Policy Distillation with a Dual-Perspective Recipe
abstract: Identifies two OPD bottlenecks: insufficient informative-state exploration and unreliable teacher supervision. Student perspective: data balancing for informative state coverage. Teacher perspective: outcome-guided margin calibration to restore order-consistency between correct/incorrect trajectories. Unified framework across LLMs and MLLMs, single/multi-teacher, strong-to-weak, cross-modal. 5 domains, 16 benchmarks.

title: The Many Faces of On-Policy Distillation: Pitfalls, Mechanisms, and Fixes
abstract: Comprehensive empirical study of OPD/OPSD failure modes: (1) distribution mismatch from student-generated prefixes; (2) optimization instability from biased TopK reverse-KL gradients; (3) OPSD fails when privileged info is instance-specific. OPSD works for shared latent rules (system prompt, alignment preference). Fixes: stop-gradient TopK objectives, RLVR-adapted teachers, SFT-stabilized students.

title: The Illusion of Certainty: Decoupling Capability and Calibration in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Identifies 'Scaling Law of Miscalibration': OPD improves accuracy but induces severe overconfidence. Root cause: teacher supervision formed under privileged training context, while deployed model has only deployment-time info—entropy collapse and systematic optimism bias. CaOPD estimates empirical confidence from rollouts and replaces self-reported confidence. Pareto-optimal calibration while maintaining accuracy.

title: Large Language Model Post-Training: A Unified View of Off-Policy and On-Policy Learning
abstract: Survey organizing post-training by trajectory provenance: off-policy (externally supplied) vs. on-policy (learner-generated rollouts). Two roles: support expansion (make useful behaviors reachable) and policy reshaping (improve within reachable regions). Consolidation role for distillation. Frames hybrid pipelines as coordinated multi-stage compositions. Comprehensive treatment of SFT, preference optimization, RL, process supervision, distillation.

title: Prefix Teach, Suffix Fade: Local Teachability Collapse in Strong-to-Weak On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Studies teachability collapse phenomenon in strong-to-weak OPD: teacher supervision becomes unreliable at suffix positions as student prefix diverges. Analyzes position-dependent reliability of teacher tokens in on-policy rollouts.

title: SOD: Step-wise On-Policy Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
abstract: Step-wise OPD for tool-integrated reasoning (TIR): erroneous tool calls cascade across reasoning steps, amplifying student-teacher divergence. SOD adaptively reweights distillation strength per step based on step-level divergence—attenuates misleading teacher signals in high-divergence regions. 0.6B student achieves 26.13% on AIME 2025, up to 20.86% improvement over second-best baseline.

title: Post-Training is About States, Not Tokens: A State Distribution View of SFT, RL, and On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Formalizes post-training as state-distribution shaping (state = prompt + generated prefix). SFT=fixed dataset states; RL/OPD=learner-induced states. Shows OPD from a degraded SFT teacher can surpass the teacher on GSM8K, TruthfulQA, MMLU. State-centric view: source and locality of training states can be as important as the supervision signal form.

title: Learning to Foresee: Unveiling the Unlocking Efficiency of On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Explains OPD efficiency as 'foresight': stable update trajectory toward final model established early. Module-allocation level: OPD identifies low-marginal-utility regions, concentrates on critical modules. Update-direction level: strong low-rank concentration with dominant subspaces aligning to final update subspace early. EffOPD: plug-and-play 3× training acceleration via adaptive extrapolation step size.

title: Learning from Language Feedback via Variational Policy Distillation
abstract: Variational policy distillation from language feedback—uses natural language critique from teacher to guide on-policy student training via a variational objective.

title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models for Autonomous Vehicle Motion Planning
abstract: Applies GKD to autonomous driving: GPT-Driver framework with on-policy GKD vs. dense-feedback RL baseline. GKD substantially outperforms RL and closely approaches teacher performance despite 5× model size reduction. Domain application demonstrating GKD generalization to trajectory prediction as language generation.

title: Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle
abstract: Reward-density principle: sparse reward for teacher-side exploration, dense OPD for student compression. 4-stage workflow: teacher RL → forward-KL warmup → on-policy distillation → optional student RL. RL-improved teacher distilled via dense bridge outperforms direct GRPO on same student (79.3% vs 75.9% MATH; 25.2% vs 19.8% AIME 2024). Each stage is load-bearing: ablations confirm.

title: Surgical Post-Training: Proximal On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning with Knowledge Retention
abstract: SPOT: addresses catastrophic forgetting in OPD. Shows KL-constrained reward formulation is critical for retention. Pipeline: Oracle corrects erroneous steps via minimal edits to generate proximal on-policy data + reward-based binary CE objective. With 4k rectified math pairs, improves Qwen3-8B by 6.2% on average, 16-min training on 8×H800. Better RL initialization.

title: Bridging Reasoning Trajectories in On-Policy Distillation via Near-Future Guidance (TOPD)
abstract: Shows 30% of high-loss OPD tokens are surface-form mismatches rather than real reasoning forks. TOPD uses near-future trajectory info to identify truly divergent states and distribute guidance across multiple future tokens. Suppressing non-divergent high-loss tokens: 47.8%→48.2%. TOPD: 52.2%, AIME24 60→63.3%, AIME25 46.7→53.3%.

title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Parameter-space analysis of OPD vs SFT vs RLVR: OPD in 'relaxed off-principal regime'—fewer affected weights, avoids principal directions more than SFT, less constrained than RLVR. OPD exhibits subspace locking: cumulative updates enter narrow low-dimensional channel early. Constraining to early update subspace preserves OPD but substantially degrades SFT. OPD induces own update geometry distinct from both SFT and RLVR.

title: OPD+: Rethinking the Advantage Design for On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Proves stop-gradient in OPD advantage estimation leads to biased reward gradient for general f-divergences. Proposes corrected OPD+ supporting various f-divergence choices beyond KL. Generic optimization framework from f-divergence between student and teacher. Validates on math reasoning and tool-use benchmarks.

title: OPRD: On-Policy Representation Distillation
abstract: Lifts OPD from output space to hidden-state space—aligns student/teacher representations across selected layers on same rollouts, bypassing LM head. Eliminates Monte Carlo KL sampling variance over large vocabularies (e.g., Qwen's ~150k tokens) and provides richer per-layer structural information. 1.44× faster training, 54% less memory vs. top-k OPD. Closes student-teacher gap on AIME 2024/2025 and AIMO where output-space OPD plateaus.

title: Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation via Peer Successes and Failures (MOPD)
abstract: MOPD: uses student's local rollout group to construct teacher signals. Conditions teacher on both successful and failed peer rollouts—successes provide positive evidence, failures provide structured negative evidence. Studies positive peer imitation and contrastive success-failure conditioning. Better instance-adaptive supervision aligned with verifier rewards on competitive programming, math, science, tool-use.

title: SimCT: Recovering Lost Supervision for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Standard OPD assumes shared tokenizer—cross-tokenizer OPD silently discards large fraction of teacher signal at vocabulary-disagreement positions. SimCT restores signal via short multi-token continuations (finest jointly-tokenizable supervision interface). Consistent gains over shared-vocab OPD and cross-tokenizer baselines on math reasoning and code generation with 3 heterogeneous teacher-student pairs.

title: When Are Teacher Tokens Reliable? Position-Weighted On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
abstract: Within-sequence position score is strongest predictor of teacher-token reliability (AUROC 0.83 vs 0.57 for entropy-only). Introduces branch-viability diagnostic to assess teacher token reliability. PW-OPSD: position-increasing weight on same rollout as OPSD. +1.0/+1.1 pts on AIME 2024/2025 Avg@12. Validates on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and Olmo-3-7B-Think.

title: f-OPD: Stabilizing Long-Horizon On-Policy Distillation with Freshness-Aware Control
abstract: Addresses asynchronous OPD: decomposes objective discrepancy into rollout drift and supervision drift. Sample-level freshness score quantifies buffered sample reliability. f-OPD adaptively regulates stale-sample influence under asynchronous training. First recipe for performance-efficiency tradeoff in OPD. Validated on reasoning, tool-use, coding-agent tasks of increasing horizon.

title: Your Teacher Can't Help You Here: Combating Supervision Fidelity Decay in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Identifies Supervision Fidelity Decay (SFD): as student-generated prefixes lengthen, teacher's token-level supervision becomes increasingly unreliable because teacher has never seen student's erroneous prefix. Proposes method to combat SFD in long-horizon reasoning distillation.

title: Are Full Rollouts Necessary for On-Policy Distillation?
abstract: Questions standard OPD's full-rollout assumption—computationally expensive and may expose to excessive compounding errors. Studies whether partial rollouts or truncated trajectories can achieve comparable performance, with implications for training efficiency.

title: Escaping the KL Agreement Trap in On-Policy Distillation
abstract: When student drifts to unrecoverable prefix, teacher locally agrees (low reverse KL) but provides little corrective signal—KL Agreement Trap. Identifies this as fundamental failure mode distinct from distribution mismatch. Proposes escape mechanism to detect and break out of agreement traps during training.

title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification
abstract: Logit-free OPD via speculative verification: avoids requirement for teacher logit access. Mitigates both off-policy distribution shift (SFT) and sparse credit assignment (RL). Uses speculative decoding-inspired verification to generate training signal without full teacher forward passes—enabling black-box-like OPD with richer signal than pure black-box methods.

title: Breaking the Tokenizer Barrier: On-Policy Distillation across Model Families
abstract: Enables standard OPD across model families with different tokenizers via precise token-mapping algorithm. Cross-tokenizer OPD significantly more compute-efficient than SFT-on-teacher-responses baseline on various benchmarks. Unlocks broader teacher-student pairs beyond same model series.

title: DP-OPD: Differentially Private On-Policy Distillation for Language Models
abstract: DP-OPD: enforces privacy only via DP-SGD on student (frozen teacher provides dense token-level targets on student-generated trajectories). Collapses private compression into single DP student-training loop. Under ε=2.0 outperforms DP fine-tuning and off-policy DP distillation, and synthesis-based DP distillation (Yelp 44.15→41.68; BigPatent 32.43→30.63 perplexity).

title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Visual Gradient Steering
abstract: Decomposes VLM OPD loss into language prior and visual grounding components. Gradient vectors nearly orthogonal—standard optimization follows suboptimal compromise. Visual Gradient Steering (VGS) dynamically reorients update vector to prioritize visual subspace. Significantly outperforms standard monolithic OPD formulation on multimodal benchmarks with minimal training overhead.

title: Draft-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Draft Models
abstract: Addresses offline-to-inference mismatch in speculative decoding draft models—SFT on target trajectories plateaus since drafter is evaluated on its own policy during inference. Draft-OPD: target-assisted rollout for stable continuations + replay from verification-exposed error positions. >5× lossless acceleration for thinking models, +23% over EAGLE-3 and +13% over DFlash.

title: ROSD: Reflective On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Model Reasoning across Domains
abstract: OPSD fails OOD: conditioning self-teacher on verified solution encourages imitation of training-domain trajectories. ROSD: self-reflector extracts corrective idea + locates first erroneous span per rollout. Corrective idea guides targeted supervision; localized error span restricts distillation to needed correction. Better in-domain reasoning and substantially better OOD generalization than standard OPSD.
